label: QNL Preservation Risk Question Set
description: Draft operational question set for file-format sustainability, obsolescence, data-loss and institutional feasibility assessment. The questions are usable for evidence collection and targeted assessment, but overall Low/Moderate/High banding is disabled until QNL validates scoring weights and thresholds.
source_basis: QNL working synthesis supplied on 2026-08-17, informed by Library of Congress sustainability concepts and National Archives and Records Administration preservation considerations
This is a QNL working question set, not an official verbatim LOC or NARA questionnaire

questions.label: Is the format specification fully disclosed and publicly accessible?
questions.definition: Assesses whether independent developers can understand and implement the format without reverse-engineering.
questions.guidance: Prefer evidence about availability and completeness of the normative specification rather than general popularity or software support.

answers.label: Full public specification supports independent implementation
Specification is partial, restricted in practice, or otherwise difficult to implement independently
Specification is unavailable or reverse-engineering is required
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Who maintains and governs the format specification?
questions.definition: Assesses whether stewardship is distributed through an open standards body or concentrated in a single vendor or owner.
questions.guidance: Consider recognized standards organizations, governance transparency, succession and continued maintenance.

answers.label: Maintained through an open or durable multi-stakeholder governance model
Governance is concentrated but maintenance and documentation remain credible
Control is concentrated, opaque, abandoned, or dependent on one commercial owner
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Is the specification stable, with manageable and backward-compatible change?
questions.definition: Assesses whether frequent major revisions or incompatible versions create preservation risk.
questions.guidance: Distinguish healthy maintenance from churn that breaks compatibility or requires repeated migrations.

answers.label: Stable specification or changes preserve practical backward compatibility
Meaningful revisions occur but remain manageable
Frequent or incompatible revisions materially threaten long-term usability
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Is rendering dependent on specific operating systems, proprietary software, or legacy hardware?
questions.definition: Assesses environmental dependencies outside the file that are required to render, validate or reuse content.
questions.guidance: Treat obsolete hardware, single-platform requirements and proprietary runtime dependencies as distinct from resources embedded within the file.

answers.label: No specialist platform dependency beyond widely available environments
Support is constrained to a limited but still maintainable environment
Rendering depends on proprietary, obsolete or specialist software/hardware environments
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Does opening or rendering the file depend on external assets or services?
questions.definition: Assesses non-embedded dependencies such as fonts, DLLs, linked spreadsheets, plugins or online endpoints.
questions.guidance: Embedded resources do not count as external dependencies merely because the format requires them to be embedded.

answers.label: The file is self-contained or uses only common non-specialist dependencies
Some external dependencies exist but can be managed or captured
Essential content depends on fragile, proprietary, remote or otherwise hard-to-preserve external assets
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Are open-source viewers, validators or extraction tools available?
questions.definition: Assesses whether the format can be rendered or inspected without relying exclusively on licensed vendor software.
questions.guidance: Consider independent implementations for reading, validation, metadata extraction and transformation.

answers.label: Multiple viable open-source or freely available implementations exist
Independent tooling exists but is incomplete or weakly maintained
Practical use depends on licensed vendor software or unavailable tooling
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: How widely adopted is the format across its target industry or creator community?
questions.definition: Assesses the breadth and durability of real-world use.
questions.guidance: Judge adoption in the format's relevant domain, while distinguishing active mainstream use from legacy prevalence.

answers.label: Widely and actively adopted in the relevant community
Adoption is domain-specific, moderate, or showing signs of concentration
Use is niche, negligible, legacy-only, or clearly declining
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Are third-party applications actively maintaining read/write support?
questions.definition: Assesses diversity and currency of independent software support.
questions.guidance: Prefer evidence of maintained implementations over historical compatibility claims.

answers.label: Multiple actively maintained applications support the format
Current support exists but is limited or concentrated
Support is legacy-only, single-implementation, or effectively absent
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Is the format formally identifiable through technical registries or standard identifiers?
questions.definition: Assesses whether the format can be reliably identified using formal registry identifiers such as PRONOM PUIDs or registered MIME types.
questions.guidance: Consider identifier specificity and automated identification support, not just the presence of a file extension.

answers.label: Formal, specific identifiers support automated identification
Registry coverage exists but is incomplete or insufficiently specific
No reliable formal identifier is available for automated identification
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Is the byte structure transparent and directly inspectable?
questions.definition: Assesses whether the representation is readily inspectable or opaque and dependent on specialized parsing.
questions.guidance: Plain text/XML is generally more transparent, but binary formats can still be well documented and preservable; use this criterion narrowly.

answers.label: Structure is directly inspectable or highly transparent
Binary structure is documented and parseable but not directly inspectable
Structure is opaque, obfuscated, or difficult to interpret independently
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: What compression mechanism is used?
questions.definition: Assesses whether encoding is uncompressed, lossless, or lossy and how that affects preservation options.
questions.guidance: Compression alone is not obsolescence; distinguish reversible lossless compression from irreversible lossy encoding.

answers.label: Uncompressed or losslessly compressed representation
Mixed or context-dependent compression requires preservation review
Lossy compression may constrain preservation or future transformation
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Would migration cause irreversible loss of essential characteristics?
questions.definition: Assesses transformation risk where decoding, recompression or conversion may irreversibly alter significant properties.
questions.guidance: Evaluate migration against documented essential characteristics rather than assuming all conversion is equivalent.

answers.label: Established migration can preserve required essential characteristics
Migration requires controlled trade-offs or careful validation
Available migration is expected to irreversibly lose essential characteristics
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Is the format subject to patents, trademark constraints, licensing fees or other IP restrictions?
questions.definition: Assesses legal or commercial constraints that can limit implementation, validation or migration tooling.
questions.guidance: Separate ordinary trademark ownership from enforceable restrictions that materially constrain preservation activity.

answers.label: No material IP restriction limits preservation implementation
Known constraints exist but appear manageable
Active restrictions or fees materially constrain preservation tooling or use
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Does the file format support or commonly contain DRM, encryption, hardcoded passwords or other TPMs that block preservation operations?
questions.definition: Assesses technological protection measures that prevent automated identification, validation, indexing or transformation.
questions.guidance: Distinguish optional security capabilities from files that are actually inaccessible without keys or credentials.

answers.label: No TPM prevents normal preservation operations
Protection is optional or can be removed through an established controlled process
DRM, encryption or credentials materially block preservation operations
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Can the format self-document through embedded technical, descriptive or structural metadata?
questions.definition: Assesses native support for embedded metadata such as EXIF, XMP or structured internal metadata.
questions.guidance: Consider both metadata capacity and whether widely used tools preserve it reliably through normal workflows.

answers.label: Strong native metadata support enables self-documentation
Embedded metadata support is limited or inconsistently preserved
Essential metadata must be maintained externally or cannot be represented
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Can accessibility features be represented and preserved natively?
questions.definition: Assesses support for text structure, alternate text, structured tables, captions or comparable accessibility semantics.
questions.guidance: Evaluate accessibility features relevant to the content type rather than requiring every feature for every format.

answers.label: Relevant accessibility semantics can be represented and preserved natively
Only part of the required accessibility semantics can be preserved
The format cannot preserve required accessibility semantics
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: For image content, can required bit depth, colour profiles and vector scale be preserved?
questions.definition: Assesses whether image-specific significant properties can be retained through storage, rendering and migration.
questions.guidance: Apply only when the assessed content is image or graphics content.

answers.label: Required image characteristics can be preserved
Some characteristics require constrained workflows or may degrade
Essential image characteristics cannot be reliably retained
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: For audio/video content, can required timecodes, multi-track audio, subtitles and related characteristics be preserved?
questions.definition: Assesses whether audiovisual significant properties remain representable and migratable.
questions.guidance: Apply only to audio or video content and assess the characteristics required by the collection policy.

answers.label: Required audiovisual characteristics can be preserved
Some characteristics require constrained workflows or may degrade
Essential audiovisual characteristics cannot be reliably retained
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: For data or spreadsheets, can explicit data types, formulas and relationships be preserved rather than flattened?
questions.definition: Assesses whether structured data semantics and computational relationships survive preservation and migration.
questions.guidance: Apply only to datasets, spreadsheets or comparable structured data content.

answers.label: Required data semantics and relationships can be preserved
Some semantics require constrained workflows or special handling
Preservation or migration would flatten or lose essential data semantics
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Does the institution possess the software infrastructure and staff expertise required to manage the format?
questions.definition: Assesses institution-specific operational capability rather than the format's global sustainability in isolation.
questions.guidance: Use institution-scoped evidence for software, validation, staffing, skills and operational support.

answers.label: Institution has routine software and staff capability
Capability exists but depends on limited staff, tooling or manual intervention
Required capability is absent or depends on unavailable specialist resources
Institutional evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Are established migration pathways and tools available?
questions.definition: Assesses whether tested preservation actions and tools exist for moving the format to sustainable alternatives when necessary.
questions.guidance: Prefer tested local pathways or evidence from preservation action registries over hypothetical conversions.

answers.label: A tested migration pathway is available
A plausible pathway exists but requires testing or manual controls
No viable migration pathway is known
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient

questions.label: Are storage and network overheads operationally sustainable for long-term preservation?
questions.definition: Assesses whether typical file sizes and preservation derivatives create material repository storage, transfer or processing constraints.
questions.guidance: Evaluate against institutional capacity and collection scale; large files are not intrinsically high risk if capacity is adequate.

answers.label: Storage, network and processing overheads are comfortably within institutional capacity
Overheads are material and require planning or optimization
Overheads exceed or threaten sustainable institutional capacity
Institutional evidence is unavailable or insufficient
